reuse.why: Reuses the existing visible-category query shape for setZero and adds one shared SQL fragment for the template rule, but does not introduce or use a single category-selection helper, so each action keeps its own query.

duplication.why: setZero gets a fourth copy of the hidden/hidden-group SELECT already pasted in the three average actions, and copyPreviousMonth applies the template rule through a separate extra query instead of the same filter.

placement.why: Everything stays in budget/actions.ts beside the actions, consistent with the tree, though the rule is spread between SQL fragments and an in-memory Set check.

scope.why: Only the month-wide actions' selection changes; single-category actions are untouched.

maintainability.why: The template condition is named once (NO_SAVED_TEMPLATE) but the hidden rule now lives in four SQL strings plus a JS check, and copyPreviousMonth uses a different mechanism, so the next rule change must again touch five places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No shared selection abstraction existed in the tree to go around; the diff extends the per-action queries.

disguised_duplication.where: copyPreviousMonth re-expresses the template rule as a separate getCategoriesWithSavedTemplates query plus Set lookup, a reshaped form of the NO_SAVED_TEMPLATE WHERE clause the other actions use.

one_place.where: The template condition is one fragment, but the month-wide selection rule as a whole (hidden, hidden group, template) is still applied separately in setZero, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg SQL and in copyPreviousMonth's JS filters.
